payload.input: Host-materialized directive for role dev (exec=subagent, claude/opus/high): implement item 6yxb3z7p (cli-ui) per its journaled scope — terminal game loop wiring engine + game-master; discharge the run contract: bun run src/cli.ts must work (healthcheck --help). Branch epic/murder-mystery-game.

payload.summary: BUG FOUND AND FIXED (src/ui/io.ts): node readline DROPS every 'line' event that arrives while no rl.question() is pending, so a piped script (bun run src/cli.ts < answers.txt) lost all but the first one or two answers and the game quit early on EOF. createStdio now keeps a standing 'line' listener that queues lines, and ask() shifts from that queue. Found only because the CLI test plays a whole game through a REAL spawned process over a REAL pipe; the in-process loop tests could never have seen it. ADR-0003's scriptability claim depended on this.

SCOPE DIVERGENCE, unresolved: the item's journaled scope names the vocabulary 'move, suggest, accuse, ask, notes, save, quit' — SAVE IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. The host build directive enumerates the loop exhaustively (roll/move, secret passage, suggest, refutation, ask, accuse, end turn) with no save and no --load flag, so building save alone would ship half a feature. Everything else in the journaled scope is built. Panel decision needed: give save/load its own item, or strike it from the scope.

TEST HAZARD, real cost incurred: a first draft of tests/ui/cli.test.ts spawned the CLI without --no-llm to prove a keyless game degrades. Blanking POE_API_KEY in the child env was NOT enough — loadLlmConfig also reads .env.local from process.cwd(), which in a spawned test IS the repo, so the suite made a LIVE call to api.poe.com and spent 2232 real tokens before it was caught. Fixed by running that one test from an mkdtemp cwd. Any future test that spawns the CLI must either pass --no-llm or run outside the repo; the env var alone does not isolate it.

UI DESIGN DECISION worth review: the numbered menu lists only what is legal in the current phase, but the FULL command vocabulary stays typable (roll, passage, suggest, accuse, ask, notes, end, quit). A word that is legal to say but not legal to do is passed to the engine, which refuses it in its own words ('p1 must be in a room to suggest'). This is what keeps the UI from holding a second, drifting copy of the rules, and it is what makes the IllegalActionError catch reachable and tested rather than defensive dead code — with menus alone, no offered option can ever be illegal.

INHERITED GAP surfaced at the UI: when EVERY llm call of a session fails, the exit ledger prints 'No LLM calls were made this session.' because SessionUsage.calls counts only COMPLETED responses (known gm/llm gap, drive k0n64xb4). The player is told nothing was spent when in fact several requests were attempted and failed. tests/ui/loop.test.ts asserts the current behaviour so the panel can see it; the fix belongs in src/llm/client.ts, not in the UI.

ENGINE WORDING QUIRK, not fixed here: describeEvent('refutation-card-shown') renders 'p1 shows you the Ballroom' — which is what the SUGGESTER should read. When the human is the REFUTER the same private event is in their log too, so after answering a suggestion the player is told 'p1 shows you the Ballroom' about their own card. The sentence needs to know which side of the event the reader is on. Engine-owned (src/engine/view.ts, item 0jrmya9a); the UI prints describeEvent verbatim by design and I did not touch it.

LIVE SMOKE (real vendor, api.poe.com, claude-sonnet-4.5): 'printf ask/1/question/quit | bun run src/cli.ts --seed 2 --players 3' produced an LLM scenario, LLM narration of the opening events, and an in-character answer from Colonel Mustard, then printed 'LLM usage: 3 calls, 3313 tokens (2668 prompt + 645 completion)' with the per-model line — token cost measured from each response's own usage object, end to end through the product surface. The 'ask' option correctly disappeared from the next menu (one question per turn).

EVIDENCE: with a human who never accuses (walks into a room, suggests, ends the turn), full offline games at 3, 4, 5 and 6 seats all reach game-over from fixed seeds in well under a second — the suspects' own deduction closes every game. 12 consecutive seeds probed, all terminated; the same seed plus the same answers replays byte-identical transcripts, and a different seed does not. That is the CLI-level confirmation of the engine's determinism and of the opponent policy's solvability.

codex
After the first vendor failure, `gm` remains active, so every later event flush retries the dead endpoint and can stall each turn for 60 seconds instead of truly degrading offline.
The required `save` command and any load/resume path are absent, so sessions cannot survive interruption and item 6yxb3z7p remains materially incomplete.
bindings.crit-agy:
Queuing incoming `stdin` lines indefinitely in `io.ts` creates a memory leak risk that could lead to an Out-Of-Memory crash if piped input arrives faster than the game consumes it.
Failing to track incomplete LLM calls in the usage ledger obscures the token costs of failed requests, creating a risk of silent budget drain during API errors.
